headline: Naidu's Amaravati offers a model for ambitious, planned urban development
content: This week’s National Interest is datelined Amaravati, the new capital N Chandrababu Naidu is building for Andhra Pradesh, just across the river Krishna from Vijayawada. It isn’t exactly about Amaravati, though. Our central theme is the idea. It’s a novelty in Indian politics, audacious in an era when no politician wants to embark on something she or he cannot complete within one term; or four years, with the fifth reserved for electioneering. Building a Capital takes much longer. One term may not be enough to flaunt it to voters as a success. And what happens if you lose power, as Mr Naidu did in 2019, just after barely collecting his first “pool” of land? His successor, Y S Jagan Mohan Reddy, and his YSRCP (Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party) called the project a sham, intended to benefit one caste, Mr Naidu’s own, since most farmers pooling land for the project were fellow Kamma. Mr Reddy scrapped the project, stopped annuity payments to farmers who had contributed their land, and declared that Andhra Pradesh would have three Capitals instead: Vizag as the executive Capital, Amaravati the legislative Capital and Kurnool the judicial Capital. Decentralisation might be an interesting idea, but not like this. Andhra Pradesh is a large state, and the distance between Vizag and Kurnool is about 700 km, with Amaravati (Vijayawada) exactly in the middle. This deserved to be called Tughlaq-like, which I did. And while Mr Reddy and his party leaders remained polite, Sakshi, the newspaper owned by his family, which had Telugu rights to publish National Interest, dropped it. That, however, is a mere sidelight in a serious discourse. Mr Naidu’s commitment is underlined by the fact that he never abandoned the idea. He promised to revive it and is now building it at warp speed. So fast, indeed, that even if there’s a change of government in the future, there will be little left to reverse. The new Capital is becoming a reality faster than electoral fortunes turn. That persistence with such an ambitious, expansive and expensive idea is what makes this project remarkable. The idea of building a new living, political, commercial, hi-tech, cultural and educational city with a soul is unfamiliar to us. We have built sarkari enclaves out of necessity: Gandhinagar, Naya Raipur, even Bhubaneswar. But these are merely seats of government. The only new city independent India has built is Chandigarh, designed for half a million people. It now has perhaps 1.4 million. That’s no city, even if it’s my hometown for all practical purposes. According to a report submitted by the Indian Institute of Human Settlements (IIHS) to the 15th Finance Commission, all cities built since Independence house no more than, hold your breath, 130 million people. These are mostly glorified colonies for ministers, legislators, officials, employees, their families and domestic workers. There’s no commerce, entrepreneurship or culture. For all that, you go to an old city nearby. Building a city, or even significantly upgrading an existing one, is an idea India has been fundamentally averse to. Why invest resources in cities when, as Gandhi told us, India lives in its villages? Those villages are so rotten in terms of quality of life, so short of opportunity and so socially unequal that millions have been leaving them for cities. Yet planned spending on cities, whether the hundreds we inherited, some dating back millennia, or those that grew chaotically into urban sprawls, was seen as a waste and a political liability. That’s why even existing cities, without exception, have decayed over time. Meanwhile, India urbanised as millions left their villages for these same cities, mostly settling in slums that the mafia gradually came to control. What’s called a slum in Mumbai goes by the name of “unauthorised colonies” in Delhi, which every political party promises to legalise. Residents are condemned to live in the same muck, with open drains. Overhanging wires and cables across the streets make them resemble a rainforest, though one made of plastic. Mumbai has been avidly cannibalising its decrepit old mills and slums. The good thing is that it’s finally building a subcity, Navi Mumbai, with the Trans-Harbour Link connecting the island city to the mainland. It’s a work in progress. Delhi employed the lazier ploy of letting large suburbs come up in Gurugram and Noida, creating a commuting and traffic nightmare as vehicles travel long distances between the three.  A large majority of Delhi’s population, however, continues to live in subhuman conditions in its unauthorised colonies. Sanjay Gandhi gave these settlements a cute name: JJ colonies, or jhuggi-jhopdi (slum and hutment). Many have been partly gentrified over time, with minimal, if any, municipal facilities. Satya Niketan, where a building collapse in September killed seven students, is one such. Bengaluru has expanded haphazardly, with the world’s worst connectivity between its city centre and economic engines. It gets flooded up to the second floor in some of its richest colonies and thirsts for water the rest of the year. The tanker mafia rules India’s Silicon Valley. And what do we say about Kolkata? Barring some new developments on the outskirts, it’s difficult to describe anything there as a slum. Most of its population still lives with a similar quality of life. Just one major Indian city bucked this trend, and it wasn’t yet a metro. Hyderabad woke up to add the muscle of tech entrepreneurship to its soul and historic spirit. It was Mr Naidu who started this during his first of four chief ministerships, beginning in 1995. He founded Cyberabad to compete with Bengaluru. His successor, Y S Rajasekhara Reddy of the Congress, carried that Telugu entrepreneurship forward, and built on it. The city didn’t just survive political change, it thrived.Mr Naidu was told by many, including much of our ‘old school’ socialist commentariat, that he had erred by focusing on the city, playing chief executive officer of the state and ignoring the poor in the process. His persistence with Amaravati, despite the 2019 electoral setback, is now seen as evidence that he’s incorrigible. And it’s a good thing. To repeat, this column isn’t about Amaravati. That deserves a full episode of “Writings On The Wall” sometime later. But a few points, especially its innovation in urbanisation, deserve mention. The biggest challenge to building infrastructure in our country is land acquisition. How come there were minimal protests in Amaravati? Mr Naidu’s first innovation was his land-pooling scheme. Farmers were invited to pool their land instead of selling it. For every acre, he committed to returning a share in developed residential and commercial plots. And what would farmers do until the Capital was built and the land monetised? Mr Naidu promised an annuity, starting at ₹50,000 per acre annually, with a 5 per cent increase every year. Today it is ₹95,000, far more than what any farmer earns from an acre. About 33,000 acres were pooled this way. The government added another 20,000 acres of its own around the planned city, taking its total area to about 53,000 acres or 217.23 square km. It’s a planned city, with grids neatly dividing it into blocks of 1 square km. Best of all, the entire government — offices, ministers, legislators, the High Court, the Vidhan Sabha and the Legislative Council, and employees of all classes — will be housed along a 7-km-long central median, occupying just 7 square km. The rest will be developed privately, with universities, tech hubs and an IBM Quantum Hub (120-qubit to begin with), scheduled for inauguration next February. This is important because governments usually consume every vacant piece of land available. Here, the government owns no more than these 7 square km. This is the second innovation. The third is a kind of political insurance. What if someone invests on the strength of your promised incentives and you lose power? Mr Naidu passed a law this week to protect investment and ensure that a share of the taxes received from these entrepreneurs went into escrow accounts, with mandatory payouts on committed dates. It’s around these political and administrative innovations that he is building this trillion-rupee city. It’s a good example for other chief ministers. Take some risks and, as he says, create wealth so the government can earn more and distribute it. By special arrangement with ThePrint

headline: Tejashwi accuses BJP MLA Maithili Thakur’s father of land grabbing
content: PATNA Leader of Opposition in Bihar Legislative Assembly Tejashwi Yadav on Friday (November 13, 2026) accused BJP MLA Maithili Thakur’s father Ramesh Thakur of forcefully encroaching private and government land. The villagers of Pokharbhinda panchayat in Darbhanga district has alleged Mr. Ramesh Thakur of encroaching on a government road and privately owned land while fencing the plot. The Deputy Collector Land Reforms (DCLR) Ajya Kumar went to the encroachment area on November 12, 2026, conducted a land survey, and then removed the illegal construction at the site. One complainant, Gagan Kumar Mishra, has written to Circle Officer (CO) on September 7, 2026, alleging Mr. Thakur of encroaching the land. “BJP MLA Maithili Thakur and her father, Ramesh Thakur, have illegally occupied government land worth hundreds of crores—along with public roads, communal ritual sites, and private plots—in the Tardih block of Darbhanga district,”Mr. Yadav wrote in social media post on X. He further said, “The administration has confirmed the authenticity of these encroachments. It is ironic, the very MLA who claimed to see a “Jungle Raj” (lawlessness) is now, under this so-called “Mangal Raj” (good governance), seizing both government and villagers’ land.” A day earlier, Ms. Thakur, who represents the Alinagar Assembly constituency, denied the charges saying that her family has valid land document. She has not reacted after the removal of the encroachment. Hitting out at Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Mr. Yadav said when a Chief Minister with criminal tendencies provides protection, his MLAs and Ministers become emboldened to commit crimes. “Targeting ordinary citizens, they have accelerated their activities by seizing government land, orchestrating the murders of government officials, engaging in corruption and moral misconduct, and intensifying extortion, robbery, and dacoity,” Mr. Yadav alleged. He also mentioned that there is no government in Bihar and tt is the NDA’s own MLAs who are now troubling the public. He further alleged that corruption and crime have crossed all limits. He asked what do Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah have to say about the “crimes and immoral acts recently committed by NDA MLAs”. He also named several other MLAs of the ruling coalition, alleging that an NDA MLA from Chirag Paswan’s Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) party, representing Belsand Assembly constituency, Amit Kumar, has seized land worth several hundred crores across the Muzaffarpur and Sitamarhi districts. “Another NDA MLA from the LJP (RV) has been implicated in the murder of the Executive Officer (EO) of the Dehri-Dalmianagar Municipal Council in Rohtas district. According to the official’s wife, the LJP (RV) MLA had her husband killed because he refused to pay a commission,” Mr. Yadav said. Executive Officer (EO) of Dalmianagar Municipal Council, Vimal Kumar, was beaten to death in Bihar’s Aurangabad district late on August 1, 2026). His wife Babita Kumari had accused Rajiv Ranjan Sing alias Sonu Singh, LJP (RV) MLA of Dehri-on-Sone, of being behind his murder. Mr. Yadav’s brother Tej Pratap Yadav has also slammed Mr. Thakur saying that illegal occupation of the land of the poor and farmers will not be tolerated at any cost. “The allegations emerging against Ramesh Thakur, the father of MLA Maithili Thakur, of land grabbing and threatening people are deeply troubling. These allegations must be investigated impartially at a high leve, “ Mr. Tej Pratap, the National President of Janshakti Janata Dal, wrote on X.

headline: Himachal approves ₹1,500 monthly financial assistance for women
content: CHANDIGARH The Himachal Pradesh government on Friday (November 13, 2026) approved the launch of the “Mukhya Mantri Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar Yojna,” under which eligible women aged 18 to 59 will receive ₹1,500 per month in financial assistance. The decision was taken in the meeting of State Cabinet held in Shimla. The meeting was chaired by Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. “It has been decided to launch the ‘Mukhya Mantri Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar Yojna’ in the State, under which eligible women in the age group of 18 to 59 years will receive financial assistance of ₹1,500 per month,” said an official statement. Under the scheme, eligible beneficiary families will also receive 300 units of free electricity, said the statement, adding “In all, 3.5 lakh eligible women have been identified as beneficiaries. The government had earlier raised the monthly assistance for women above 59 years from ₹1,050 to ₹1,500.” Providing financial assistance of ₹1,500 monthly to women between 18 to 60 years of age and giving free electricity upto 300 units monthly to households were among the key pre-poll promises made by the Congress party during the 2022 Assembly election. The Cabinet also decided to adopt a uniform State policy for determining and periodically revising the rates for the sale of surplus raw water to neighbouring States, government agencies and industries. “Under the policy, an initial benchmark rate of ₹100 per 1,000 cubic feet will be applicable to all existing and future projects of the State, including inter-State water projects. The rates will be revised periodically in accordance with the prescribed mechanism linked to the Wholesale Price Index (WPI),” the statement added. It was also decided to launch the ‘Khelo Himachal Chitta Mukt Abhiyan-2026’ across all twelve districts of the State. The initiative aims to engage youth in sports activities and strengthen efforts towards drug prevention by promoting a healthy lifestyle, discipline and positive community participation. Meanwhile, in Mandi, the Chief Minister led the anti ‘chitta’ (heroin) awareness walkathon, urging the people to participate in the fight against drug abuse and help make the State drug-free. Addressing a public gathering, he said “I want to make it absolutely clear that there is no place in Himachal Pradesh for those who sell ‘chitta’ and destroy the lives of our youth for money. The government had adopted a firm policy against those involved in the illegal drug trade and that strict legal action was being taken against drug peddlers and traffickers.”

headline: FIR against Kangana Ranaut over X post on Gandhi family deaths
content: SHIMLA: Shimla Police on Friday night registered an FIR against BJP MP from Mandi Kangana Ranaut after a local resident filed a complaint with Himachal Pradesh DGP Ashok Tewari over her social media post that allegedly contains grave insinuations concerning the deaths of former Prime Ministers Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi, and Indira’s son Sanjay Gandhi.Shimla SSP Gaurav Singh said an FIR had been registered against Kangana over alleged objectionable posts on the Gandhi family.In his complaint, Captain Atul Sharma (retd.) has objected to a social media post published on Kangana’s verified account @KanganaTeam on Nov 10. The complainant alleged that it juxtaposes the deaths of the three Gandhi family members with Sonia Gandhi’s subsequent political rise, and uses the expression: “How convenient!” He claimed that the narrative could create misleading impressions.The complaint seeks scrutiny of “potentially inflammatory and unsubstantiated imputations” capable of disturbing public tranquillity. Sharma has urged police to examine the posts under BNS Sections 196 (promoting enmity between different groups) and 353 (making, publishing, or circulating false information, rumours with the intent to cause fear, alarm, or public disorder).Sharma seeks a cyber forensic examination to establish their authenticity, context and dissemination.TOI tried to contact Kangana and her team but there was no response.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Leads Anti-Drug Walkathon in Mandi
content: Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday spearheaded an anti-'chitta' awareness walkathon in Mandi, calling for a united front against drug abuse to eradicate the menace and foster a drug-free state.Information was available with The Chenab Times that the walkathon commenced from Paddal Ground, traversing through the bus stand and Seri Manch before concluding back at its origin. The event saw significant participation from students and local residents. Chief Minister Sukhu administered an anti-'chitta' pledge to the attendees, urging their active involvement in the ongoing campaign.Addressing the assembled crowd, Chief Minister Sukhu emphasized that while the government is implementing sustained and stringent measures against the drug trade, enforcement alone is insufficient to combat the problem. He stressed the necessity of collective participation from families, educators, panchayats, mahila mandals, yuvak mandals, and the youth to effectively tackle drug abuse.“There is no place in Himachal Pradesh for those who sell 'chitta' and destroy the lives of our youth for pecuniary gain,” Sukhu stated, reaffirming the government's commitment to taking strict legal action against drug peddlers and traffickers.Highlighting the government's proactive crackdown on illicit activities, the Chief Minister reported that 22 properties built on government land have been vacated and demolished during the current administration's tenure. Furthermore, assets valued at Rs 92 crore, purportedly acquired through illegal drug operations, have been seized.The Chief Minister appealed to the public not to remain silent regarding drug-related activities. He urged citizens to share credible information about drug traffickers with the authorities by utilizing the emergency toll-free number 112. He also noted that provisions have been established to offer rewards to individuals who provide accurate information leading to the apprehension of drug traffickers.The campaign, which was initiated approximately a year ago, has garnered substantial public support across various districts, including Shimla, Dharamsala, Hamirpur, Una, and Bilaspur. The Chief Minister observed that the enthusiastic participation in Mandi further underscores the growing collective resolve to combat the drug menace.Reiterating his government's unwavering commitment, Sukhu declared that Himachal Pradesh would not permit 'chitta' to compromise the future of its youth.

headline: Centre tightens winter pollution controls in Delhi-NCR, orders sealing of 191 units
content: With winter pollution intensifying in Delhi-NCR, Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav has directed the states of Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan to step up enforcement of pollution control measures, warning of action against officials and agencies failing to meet deadlines.Chairing a review meeting on Saturday, Yadav directed the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) to immediately seal 191 identified polluting industries that have not even placed orders for installing Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs), despite repeated directions.He also warned that the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) would initiate criminal prosecution against Transport Department officials in states that fail to install Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras by November 30.Emphasising that air pollution does not recognise state boundaries, the Minister called for coordinated and time-bound enforcement across the National Capital Region (NCR), moving beyond planning to visible action on the ground.The states were directed to nominate Secretary-level officers for 15 cities — seven in Haryana, four in Uttar Pradesh and four in Rajasthan — to oversee pollution control measures through field inspections and submit weekly progress reports to the CAQM. The commission was asked to issue notices to non-performing officers.Yadav said more than 30 review meetings had been held with NCR state governments and municipal bodies over the past year to strengthen pollution preparedness and implementation of action plans.Reviewing road dust management, the Minister noted that only 3,221 km of the targeted 5,480 km of roads had been redeveloped. He directed agencies to expedite pothole repairs, pave road shoulders and central verges, intensify mechanical sweeping and undertake deep-cleaning drives. Traffic congestion at 233 identified points across NCR was also flagged for immediate attention.The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) was asked to complete the installation of Multi-Lane Free Flow systems at 154 Delhi border entry points by December 31.On vehicular pollution, Yadav called for expediting the PARIVARTAN scheme to replace pre-BS-VI trucks and buses with BS-VI, CNG and electric vehicles by 2028. States were also asked to accelerate the installation of ANPR-based monitoring systems at fuel stations, linked to VAHAN and pollution-under-control certificate databases.Of the 2,345 targeted industries in NCR, 2,298 (98 per cent) have been connected to Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS). The Minister stressed strict enforcement of the particulate matter emission limit of 50 mg/Nm³, with closure, electricity disconnection and sealing of non-compliant units.He also directed states to bridge the 6,747-tonne-per-day gap in municipal solid waste processing capacity, prevent open dumping and burning, and expedite the clearance of legacy waste at Okhla, Ghazipur, Bhalswa and Bandhwari.The Minister called for focused hotspot action plans covering markets, schools, hospitals, railway stations and bus terminals, besides strict implementation of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) and winter action plans.Highlighting technology-led monitoring, Yadav cited Delhi's Integrated Command and Control Centre and CAQM's PAVAN platform for real-time tracking of pollution, emissions and compliance. He also called for greater public participation through awareness campaigns involving resident welfare associations, transport bodies and the construction industry.Yadav, along with state environment ministers, will undertake regular field inspections to assess implementation of the measures.

headline: Paddy politics: Chhattisgarh government’s per-acre aid blunts Congress
content: RAIPUR: Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai’s government is preparing to launch its statewide mega-procurement drive on November 15, coinciding with Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas.In a calculated policy manoeuvre that political observers view as an early salvo for the 2028 Assembly elections, the Sai cabinet has decided to disburse a flat input assistance of Rs 13,839 per acre even to farmers whose harvest falls short of the 21-quintal-per-acre procurement ceiling.The timing of the announcement—just ahead of BJP National President Nitin Nabin’s high-profile visit to Dharamjaigarh (Raigarh district) for the November 15 tribal pride celebrations—underscores its political weight. By decoupling the full bonus benefit from actual yield volume, the ruling BJP aims to neutralise Congress’s traditional rural plank while delivering direct financial relief to over 27.5 lakh registered farmer families, particularly small and marginal cultivators in tribal-dominated Bastar and Surguja regions where per-acre productivity is lower.Previously, farmers suffering low yields were forced to buy paddy from middlemen and rice millers at Rs 2,100 to Rs 2,400 per quintal just to fill their 21-quintal quota and claim the full state bonus. After factoring in transport and ancillary costs, farmers were left with a meagre Rs 400 to Rs 500 margin while brokers pocketed the lion's share. Under the revised mechanism, the state will transfer the input assistance directly into farmers' bank accounts based on verified cultivated area—eliminating the compulsion to arrange extra grain and choking off illegal paddy inflow..Backed by an administrative push led by CM Sai, Agriculture Minister Ramvichar Netam, and Agriculture Production Commissioner Siddharth Komal Singh Pardeshi, the state has finalised logistical and digital upgrades for the 2026–27 Kharif marketing season.Purchases will run at Rs 3,100 per quintal (up to 21 quintals per acre) across 3,100 procurement centres, including 360 newly opened centres designed to cut travel time and congestion.Farmers registered last year with an AgriStack ID require no fresh registration. The mandatory submission of loan passbooks at cooperative societies has been scrapped, replaced by digital crop surveys and biometric authentication to ensure airtight transparency.Over the past three marketing years (2023–26), the state procured roughly 437 lakh metric tonnes of paddy, disbursing nearly Rs 1.50 lakh crore to farmers.The policy shift has triggered an immediate war of words between the ruling party and the opposition. Former Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel dismissed the Rs 13,839 per-acre input assistance as a mere extension of his previous Congress government's flagship scheme.Demanding a White Paper on procurement readiness, gunny bag (bardana) availability, storage, payments, and rice lifting, Baghel also alleged that the ongoing patwari strike has derailed farmer registrations and crop damage surveys.Hitting back sharply, Forest Minister Kedar Kashyap accused the Congress of playing petty politics over agrarian welfare while failing to honour its own past promises.Kashyap asserted that the Rs 13,839 guaranteed aid would be a game-changer for low-yield tribal belts in Bastar and Surguja, leaving the opposition rattled as its core electoral narrative slips away..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Karnataka mandates gynaecological check-ups for girls, sex education in schools
content: Bengaluru The Karnataka government has recently issued a joint circular, with multiple concerned departments on board, on measures to ensure the well-being of students across all schools, colleges, hostels, residential schools, and training institutions in the State. These measures include conducting mandatory check-ups for all girls in schools by a gynaecologist, the provision of sex education, and the creation of awareness among children regarding child rights, issues concerning teenage pregnancies, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, child marriage, and the Child Helpline (1098). Furthermore, the installation of CCTV cameras has been made mandatory in all schools and colleges. Technical Education Dept. asks Karnataka colleges to take measures to protect adolescent students from abuse and exploitation Technical Education Dept. asks Karnataka colleges to take measures to protect adolescent students from abuse and exploitation This follows recommendation by the Karnataka State Commission for Protection of Child Rights Technical Education Dept. asks Karnataka colleges to take measures to protect adolescent students from abuse and exploitation storyline 1 A warning has also been issued stating that failure to prevent — or negligence in addressing — cases of child marriage, teenage pregnancy, and incidents falling under the POCSO Act, 2012, will result in both legal action and disciplinary proceedings against the officials concerned. The circular is a culmination of a series of measures initiated in June 2025 over concerns about rising cases of child marriage and teenage pregnancy in the State. Child Protection Committee Among the measures prescribed is the formation of Child Protection Committees in educational institutions across the State. The committee, comprising parents, children, and teachers, must meet once every three months, and the proceedings of these meetings should be duly recorded, the circular noted. Schools and residential schools must install complaint boxes and take measures to address the grievances of girl students. It has been mandated that experienced and qualified counsellors be appointed in schools and Pre-University (PU) colleges to address the mental health and other challenges faced by adolescent students. Teachers must persuade parents to re-enrol girls who have dropped out of school and ensure that they continue their education until the age of 18. They must also take measures to prevent school-going children from being subjected to child labour. Children should be provided with appropriate education to help them understand and identify issues such as crimes against children, child labour, child trafficking, sexual abuse, and child marriage through both formal and informal educational curricula. They should also be taught to recognise any form of abuse, violence, discrimination, or exploitation directed against them, whether within educational institutions or elsewhere, the circular said. “If a girl student in a school or residential school remains absent for more than three days without providing any notification, the principal must inform the gram panchayat and the child helpline (1098) in writing. The Health Department has stated that appropriate legal action must be taken against shops selling abortion pills without a doctor’s prescription, as well as against doctors and members of the public involved in unauthorised abortion activities,” the circular said. Substance abuse Additionally, the guidelines emphasise the need to raise awareness among children about the dangers of substance abuse and drug addiction, alongside conducting regular screenings for such issues. They stipulate that such awareness should also be integrated into the school curriculum.

headline: India’s Assam state demolishes homes of 132 Muslim families
content: Authorities in India’s Assam have demolished the homes of 132 Muslim families, citing illegal encroachment on government land. Residents say they were settled there after fleeing the 1983 anti-Muslim riots. Researchers say the evictions have disproportionately targeted Bengali-origin Muslims.

headline: No place in Himachal for those selling chitta: Sukhu | Hindustan Times
content: Himachal Pradesh chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday led the anti-chitta awareness walkathon in Mandi and appealed to the people of the state, particularly the youth, to actively participate in the fight against drug abuse and help make the state drug-free.The walkathon started from Paddal Ground, proceeded towards the bus stand and Seri Manch, and returned to Paddal Ground. A large number of students and local residents from across the district participated in the walkathon. On the occasion, the CM administered the anti-chitta pledge to the participants and urged them to remain alert and contribute actively to the campaign against drug abuse.Addressing a public gathering at Paddal Ground, the CM said that the state government was taking strict and continuous action against the drug trade. He stressed that the problem could not be tackled through government and police action alone, and required the active support and cooperation of every section of society.“I want to make it absolutely clear that there is no place in Himachal Pradesh for those who sell chitta and destroy the lives of our youth for money. The government had adopted a firm policy against those involved in the illegal drug trade and that strict legal action was being taken against drug peddlers and traffickers,” he said. The CM said that during the present government’s tenure, 22 properties constructed on government land had been vacated and demolished. In addition, assets worth ₹92 crore, allegedly acquired through illegal drug activities, had been seized so far.Seeking collective support, the CM said that the fight against drugs required the participation of every mother, father, teacher, panchayat, mahila mandal, yuva mandal and above all the youth of the state. He urged support of every section of society in this fight. “Today, I am entrusting this responsibility to the youth of the state,” he said.On the occasion, the CM also laid the foundation stone of the District Library building in Mandi, which will be constructed at a cost of ₹6.55 crore.

headline: Kangana Ranaut booked for defamation over social media post targeting Sonia Gandhi | Hindustan Times
content: Shimla police on Friday booked BJP MP from Mandi, Kangana Ranaut, under charges of defamation and promoting enmity between different groups, following a complaint filed by a Shimla resident to Himachal Pradesh director general of police (DGP), seeking registration of an FIR against the MP over her social media posts concerning the Gandhi family.Shimla superintendent of police (SP) Gaurav Singh confirmed the first information report (FIR) registered under Sections 353 (statements conducing to public mischief), 356 (defamation) and 196 (promoting enmity between different groups on ground of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, etc., and doing acts prejudicial to maintenance of harmony) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).In a complaint sent on November 12 to the Himachal DGP, Capt. Atul Sharma sought a cyber forensic examination of posts published on November 10 on Ranaut’s verified X account (@KanganaTeam) accompanying an archival video of the Gandhi family.The complainant alleged that the X posts contained insinuations concerning the deaths of former Prime Ministers Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi, and Congress leader Sanjay Gandhi while portraying Sonia Gandhi as a “mysterious foreign national”.The complaint alleged that Ranaut’s posts juxtaposed the deaths of the three members of the Gandhi family with Sonia Gandhi’s subsequent political prominence.It also refers to remarks allegedly made by Ranaut about Maneka Gandhi being expelled from the family residence following Sanjay Gandhi’s death, and the use of the expression “how convenient” in the context of the deaths and subsequent political developments.

headline: 'Mysterious Foreign National': Himachal Police Book BJP MP Kangana Ranaut Over X Post Against Sonia Gandhi
content: Himachal Pradesh Police have registered a First Information Report (FIR) against Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Member of Parliament from Mandi, Kangana Ranaut, over allegedly inflammatory social media posts targeting the Gandhi family. Confirmed by Shimla Superintendent of Police Gaurav Singh, the case was lodged at the Boileauganj police station in Shimla under Sections 196, 353, and 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023—provisions covering the promotion of enmity between groups, public mischief through false information, and defamation. The police action follows a formal complaint submitted by retired Army officer Captain Atul Sharma, who initially emailed his grievance to Director General of Police Ashok Tewari before recording his official statement at the Boileauganj station. Officers have initiated a formal probe and begun collecting digital records linked to the disputed content. What Triggered the Police Complaint According to the complaint, the controversy centres on a post published on November 10 from Ranaut’s verified account on social media platform X. The post allegedly linked the tragic deaths of former Prime Ministers Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi, along with Sanjay Gandhi, to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s subsequent political rise. In his submission, Sharma noted that the post characterised Sonia Gandhi as a “mysterious foreign national” who entered the family before relatives were killed one after another, concluding with the remark, “How convenient”. The message also referenced the alleged expulsion of Maneka Gandhi from the family residence following Sanjay Gandhi’s death. Sharma contended that such insinuations cross the boundary of legitimate political criticism and risk inciting public hostility and disturbing social harmony. Cyber-Forensic Probe Sought Amid Political Reactions Along with copies and direct URLs of the November 10 post, the complainant has urged police to preserve electronic metadata and conduct a time-bound cyber-forensic examination to authenticate the material and trace its digital dissemination. Meanwhile, senior Himachal Pradesh Congress leaders, including Chief Minister’s Principal Advisor (Media) Naresh Chauhan, strongly condemned the Mandi MP’s remarks as irresponsible and divisive. Ranaut and her office have yet to issue an official response regarding the registration of the FIR as investigators proceed with verifying the electronic evidence.

headline: "Personal opinion, not party’s official statement": Himachal BJP distances itself from Kangana Ranaut’s social media remarks
content: Dharamshala (Himachal Pradesh) [India], November 14 (ANI): Himachal Pradesh Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) spokesperson Sanjay Sharma on Saturday distanced the party from recent social media posts made by Mandi MP Kangana Ranaut regarding Congress leader Sonia Gandhi and the Gandhi family, asserting that her online statements reflect her individual views rather than the party's formal stance.Speaking to ANI in Dharamshala, Sharma emphasised that the BJP has designated official spokespersons at both the state and national levels to communicate its formal position."Kangana Ranaut is the Member of Parliament from the BJP's Mandi parliamentary constituency. Whatever she says or writes on her social media platform is her personal opinion and not the party's official statement," Sharma said, reiterating that the party operates along a defined line and that individual remarks online cannot be treated as the BJP's official view.The clarification comes a day after Himachal Pradesh Police registered a First Information Report (FIR) at the Shimla West police station against Ranaut under Sections 196, 353, and 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The case followed a complaint by Shimla resident retired Captain Atul Sharma alleging that Ranaut’s November 10 social media post contained inflammatory and misleading insinuations about the deaths of Gandhi family members and referred to Sonia Gandhi as a "mysterious foreign national".Addressing the legal proceedings in Shimla, Sharma stated that the FIR was a matter between the complainant and the Mandi MP, adding that the court would examine the facts and determine the truth. Referring to Ranaut's work on the film Emergency and various books written on historical events—including controversies surrounding Sanjay Gandhi's death—he noted that she appeared to have conducted her own research and maintained that the judiciary would ultimately decide on the matter.At the same time, the BJP spokesperson launched a counter-attack against the Congress party over its criticism of Ranaut, accusing the opposition of double standards regarding the dignity of women and citing past derogatory remarks directed at her during election campaigning."When Kangana Ranaut came to contest the election, a Congress spokesperson made a statement about the 'going rates' in Mandi. Later, a state Congress minister remarked that if you remove the makeup from Kangana Ranaut's face, there is nothing left to look at," Sharma alleged, questioning whether a woman candidate did not deserve respect.Claiming that neither the Congress spokesperson nor the state minister was removed, and that no senior or state Congress leader apologised despite widespread hurt caused by those comments, Sharma demanded accountability from the opposition. "To truly honour women, the Congress should not look at just one woman, but respect all women. The Congress party must answer for this," he said. (ANI)

headline: Himachal CM leads anti-chitta walkathon in Mandi
content: Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday led an anti-chitta awareness walkathon in Mandi, urging people, particularly the youth, to unite against drug abuse and help make the state drug-free.The walkathon began at Paddal Ground, proceeded towards the bus stand and Seri Manch before returning to its starting point, with a large number of students and local residents participating. Sukhu administered the anti-chitta pledge and called upon participants to actively contribute to the campaign.Addressing the gathering, the Chief Minister said the government was taking sustained and stringent action against the drug trade but stressed that enforcement alone could not eliminate the menace. He called for collective participation from families, teachers, panchayats, mahila mandals, yuvak mandals and the youth.“There is no place in Himachal Pradesh for those who sell chitta and destroy the lives of our youth for money,” Sukhu said, asserting that strict legal action was being taken against drug peddlers and traffickers.Highlighting the government’s crackdown, he said 22 properties constructed on government land had been vacated and demolished during the present government’s tenure. Assets worth Rs 92 crore, allegedly acquired through illegal drug activities, had also been seized.Appealing to people not to remain silent about drug-related activities, Sukhu urged them to share credible information with authorities through the emergency toll-free number 112. He added that provisions had been made to reward those providing accurate information about drug traffickers.The Chief Minister said the campaign, launched nearly a year ago, had received strong public support in Shimla, Dharamsala, Hamirpur, Una and Bilaspur. The participation witnessed in Mandi, he said, reflected the growing resolve to fight the drug menace.Reaffirming his government’s commitment, Sukhu said Himachal Pradesh would not allow chitta to destroy the future of its youth.

headline: CM Sukhu leads anti-chitta walkathon in Mandi, calls for people’s movement against drugs
source: Achievements of Atal Medical and Research University
content: Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday led the anti-chitta awareness walkathon in Mandi and appealed to the people of Himachal Pradesh, particularly the youth, to actively participate in the fight against drug abuse and help make the State drug-free. The walkathon started from Paddal Ground to Seri Manch and returned back to Paddal Ground. A large number of local residents from across the district participated . Thousands of enthusiastic students from different schools dressed in their school uniforms, raising slogans against the drug abuse, especially Chitta, were the main attraction of the walkathon. The CM administered an Anti-chitta pledge to the participants and urged them to remain alert and contribute actively to the campaign against drug abuse. Addressing a public gathering at Paddal Ground, the Chief Minister said, “The state government was taking strict and continuous action against the illegal drug trade and stressed on the need of active public participation in the campaign as this is a social problem and cannot be tackled only by police action alone and required the active support and cooperation of every section of society.” He said , “ I want to make it absolutely clear that there is no place in Himachal Pradesh for those who sell chitta and destroy the lives of our youth for money and strict legal action is being taken against drug peddlers and traffickers” .

headline: Himachal Pradesh Government
content: Central government's transformative initiatives strengthening India's global standing, paving way for Viksit Bharat@2047 Says Himachal holds immense potential to expand its global trade and investment footprint Calls upon IBCCI to connect Indian entrepreneurs with Global Markets and Investment Opportunities Himachal Pradesh Governor Kavinder Gupta said that India, under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has emerged as a confident, self-reliant and trusted global economic partner, with the central government's transformative policies opening new avenues for investment, innovation, entrepreneurship and international trade. The Governor was addressing the Indian Global Partnership Programme, organised by the International Business Chamber of Commerce and Industry (IBCCI) in New Delhi, today. The IBCCI organised ‘India Global Partnerships' on Women Entrepreneurship and Startups@ Viksit Bharat 2047 and participating countries were Brazil, South Africa, Fiji, Mongolia, Suriname and Guyana. Addressing the gathering, the Governor said that India's remarkable economic transformation reflects the Prime Minister's unwavering commitment to strengthening the nation's capabilities and enhancing its standing on the global stage.
